description: Reference period stored as a date. In quarterly_government_operations.csv it is the first day of the calendar quarter (1990-01-01 is the first quarter of 1990, 2026-04-01 is the second quarter of 2026). In annual_consolidated_government_finances.csv it is January 1 of the reference year (2007-01-01 to 2024-01-01), where the official notes say the year means the end of the fiscal year closest to December 31.

Geography as published. The quarterly file has Canada only. The annual file has Canada plus each province and territory for consolidated provincial, territorial and local governments, and Canada only for consolidated Canadian general government.
Statistics Canada Dissemination Geography Unique Identifier for the geography.

Quarterly file only. Government sector as published: Consolidated government, Federal government, Provincial and territorial government, Local government (which includes Indigenous governments), or Canada Pension Plan (CPP) and Quebec Pension Plan (QPP).

Line of the statement of operations or balance sheet as published, for example Revenue, Taxes, Expense, Interest, Net operating balance, Net lending or borrowing, Financial assets, Liabilities or Net financial worth. In the annual file the official Government Finance Statistics classification codes are kept in square brackets. Child lines are parts of their parent lines, so do not add parents and children together.
Unit of measure for value, as published: Dollars.
Statistics Canada numeric code for the unit of measure.
Scale of value as published: millions. A value of 1000 means 1,000 million dollars, or 1 billion dollars.
Statistics Canada numeric code for the scalar factor.
Statistics Canada vector identifier for the series. Useful if you want to pull the same series again.
Statistics Canada coordinate string that locates the series inside the official table.

The published value in millions of current dollars. Empty when Statistics Canada did not publish a figure (status ..). Negative values are deficits, net borrowing, or net liabilities where the line item is a balance. Official values were not altered.
Statistics Canada status symbol. .. means not available for that reference period and value is empty. Empty status means a regular published value.
Annual file: r means revised and p means preliminary, as published. Empty when no symbol was given.
t if Statistics Canada has terminated this series, otherwise empty.
Number of decimal places Statistics Canada uses when displaying the value.
